items.stem: From the top of a 15 m high building, the angle of elevation of the top of a tower is found to be 30°. From the bottom of the same building, the angle of elevation of the top of the tower is found to be 60°. Find the height of the tower and the distance between tower and the building.
items.answer: Let the tower be AB of height h and let d be the horizontal distance between the tower and the 15 m building. Seen from the foot of the building, tan 60° = h/d, so h = √3 d. Seen from the top of the building the tower rises only (h − 15) above eye level, so tan 30° = (h − 15)/d, that is d = √3 (h − 15). Substituting d, h = √3 × √3 (h − 15) = 3h − 45, hence 2h = 45 and h = 22.5 m. Then d = 22.5/√3 = 45/(2√3) = 15√3/2 ≈ 12.99 m. The tower is 22.5 m high and stands about 12.99 m from the building.
items.section_heading: FIVE MARKS QUESTIONS | Board 2024 OD Standard

items.stem: The angles of depression of the top and bottom of an 8 m tall building from top of a multi-storeyed building are 30° and 45°, respectively. Find the height of multi-storey building and distance between two buildings.
items.answer: Let the multi-storeyed building AB have height h and let x be the distance between the two buildings. The foot of the 8 m building is seen at a depression of 45°, so tan 45° = h/x, giving x = h. The top of the 8 m building is seen at a depression of 30°, and it lies (h − 8) below the top of the tall building, so tan 30° = (h − 8)/x, giving x = √3 (h − 8). Equating, h = √3 h − 8√3, so h(√3 − 1) = 8√3 and h = 8√3/(√3 − 1) = 4√3(√3 + 1) = (12 + 4√3) m = 4(3 + √3) m ≈ 18.93 m. Since x = h, the distance between the buildings is also 4(3 + √3) m. Hence the multi-storeyed building is 4(3 + √3) m high and the buildings are 4(3 + √3) m apart.
items.section_heading: FIVE MARKS QUESTIONS | Board Term-2 OD 2014

items.stem: The angle of elevation of an aeroplane from a point on the ground is 60°. After a flight of 30 seconds the angle of elevation becomes 30°. If the aeroplane is flying at a constant height of 3000√3 m, find the speed of the aeroplane.
items.answer: Let E be the point of observation and let the plane fly from A to B at the constant height AD = BC = 3000√3 m. In right triangle AED, tan 60° = AD/DE, so √3 = 3000√3/DE and DE = 3000 m. In right triangle BEC, tan 30° = BC/EC, so 1/√3 = 3000√3/(DE + DC), giving DE + DC = 3000√3 × √3 = 9000 m. Hence DC = 9000 − 3000 = 6000 m, and this is the distance flown in 30 seconds. Speed = 6000/30 = 200 m/s = 200 × 18/5 = 720 km/h. The aeroplane is flying at 720 km/h.
items.section_heading: FIVE MARKS QUESTIONS | Board 2020 SQP Standard, 2014

items.stem: The person standing on the bank of river observes that the angle of elevation of the top of a tree standing on opposite bank is 60°. When he moves 30 m away from the bank, he finds the angle of elevation to be 30°. Find the height of tree and width of the river.
items.answer: Let CD be the tree of height h, let B be the point on the bank with BC = x the width of the river, and let A be the position 30 m behind B. In right triangle DBC, tan 60° = h/x, so h = √3 x. In right triangle DAC, tan 30° = h/(x + 30), so √3 h = x + 30. Substituting h = √3 x gives 3x = x + 30, hence x = 15 m. Then h = 15√3 = 15 × 1.732 ≈ 25.98 m. The tree is about 25.98 m high and the river is 15 m wide.
items.section_heading: FIVE MARKS QUESTIONS | Board 2020 OD Basic

items.stem: A vertical tower stands on horizontal plane and is surmounted by a vertical flag-staff of height 6 m. At a point on the ground, angle of elevation of the bottom and top of the flag-staff are 30° and 45° respectively. Find the height of the tower. (Take √3 = 1.73)
items.answer: Let BD be the tower of height h and DA the flag-staff of height 6 m, observed from the point C on the ground with BC the horizontal distance. The top A is seen at 45°, so tan 45° = AB/BC, that is 1 = (h + 6)/BC, hence BC = h + 6. The bottom D is seen at 30°, so tan 30° = DB/BC, that is 1/√3 = h/(h + 6). Cross-multiplying, h√3 = h + 6, so h(√3 − 1) = 6 and h = 6/(√3 − 1) = 6(√3 + 1)/2 = 3(√3 + 1) = 3(1.73 + 1) = 3 × 2.73 = 8.19 m. The tower is 8.19 m high.
items.section_heading: FIVE MARKS QUESTIONS | Board 2020 Delhi Standard

items.stem: From a point on the ground, the angles of elevation of the bottom and the top of a tower fixed at the top of a 20 m high building are 45° and 60° respectively. Find the height of the tower.
items.answer: Let AB be the 20 m building and BD the tower standing on it, observed from the point P on the ground. The bottom B is seen at 45°, so tan 45° = AB/AP, that is 1 = 20/AP and AP = 20 m. The top D is seen at 60°, so tan 60° = AD/AP = (20 + BD)/20, giving √3 = (20 + BD)/20, hence 20 + BD = 20√3 and BD = 20√3 − 20 = 20(√3 − 1) = 20(1.732 − 1) = 20 × 0.732 = 14.64 m. The tower is 14.64 m high.
items.section_heading: FIVE MARKS QUESTIONS | Board 2020 OD Standard

items.stem: From the top of a 7 m high building the angle of elevation of the top of a tower is 60° and the angle of depression of its foot is 45°. Determine the height of the tower.
items.answer: Let AB be the 7 m building and CD the tower, with x the horizontal distance between them. Draw AE horizontal from the top A of the building to meet the tower at E, so AE = BD = x and ED = AB = 7 m. The foot D is seen at a depression of 45°, so tan 45° = AB/BD, that is 1 = 7/x and x = 7 m. The top C is seen at an elevation of 60°, so tan 60° = CE/AE, that is √3 = CE/x, giving CE = 7√3 m. Hence CD = CE + ED = 7√3 + 7 = 7(1 + √3) = 7 × 2.732 ≈ 19.12 m. The tower is about 19.12 m high.
items.section_heading: FIVE MARKS QUESTIONS | Board 2020 Delhi Standard

items.stem: Two poles of equal heights are standing opposite to each other on either side of the road which is 80 m wide. From a point P between them on the road, the angle of elevation of the top of a pole is 60° and the angle of depression from the top of the other pole of point P is 30°. Find the heights of the poles and the distance of the point P from the poles.
items.answer: Let both poles have height h, let AB be the pole whose top is seen from P at 30° (the depression of P from that top is 30°, so the elevation of that top from P is also 30°), and let CD be the pole whose top is seen at 60°. Put PB = x, so PC = 80 − x. In right triangle ABP, tan 30° = h/x, so h = x/√3. In right triangle CDP, tan 60° = h/(80 − x), so h = √3(80 − x). Equating, x/√3 = √3(80 − x), that is x = 3(80 − x), so 4x = 240 and x = 60 m. Then h = 60/√3 = 20√3 = 34.64 m. Each pole is 34.64 m high; P is 60 m from the pole seen at 30° and 80 − 60 = 20 m from the pole seen at 60°.
items.ocr: The printed closing lines read 'Distance of point P from pole AB is 20 m. Distance of point P from pole CD is 60 m', which contradicts the same solution's own x = PB = 60 m for the pole AB subtending 30°. Following the worked solution: P is 60 m from the 30° pole (AB) and 20 m from the 60° pole (CD).

items.stem: Two poles of equal heights are standing opposite to each other on either side of a road, which is 80 m wide. From a point between them on the road, angles of elevation of their top are 30° and 60°. Find the height of the poles and distance of point from poles.
items.answer: Let both poles have height h and let E be the point on the road, with BE = x the distance to the pole AB seen at 30°, so ED = 80 − x is the distance to the pole CD seen at 60°. In right triangle ABE, tan 30° = h/x, so h = x/√3. In right triangle CDE, tan 60° = h/(80 − x), so h = √3(80 − x) = 80√3 − x√3. Equating, x/√3 = 80√3 − x√3, that is x = 240 − 3x, so 4x = 240 and x = 60 m. Then h = 60/√3 = 20√3 ≈ 34.64 m. Each pole is about 34.64 m high, and the point is 60 m from the pole seen at 30° and 20 m from the pole seen at 60°.
items.section_heading: FIVE MARKS QUESTIONS | Board 2019 Delhi, OD 2011

items.stem: Amit, standing on a horizontal plane, find a bird flying at a distance of 200 m from him at an elevation of 30°. Deepak standing on the roof of a 50 m high building, find the angle of elevation of the same bird to be 45°. Amit and Deepak are on opposite sides of the bird. Find the distance of the bird from Deepak.
items.answer: Let O be the bird, A be Amit on the ground with OA = 200 m at an elevation of 30°, and let D be Deepak on the roof of the 50 m building FD. Drop OL perpendicular to the ground and let M be the foot of the perpendicular from O to the horizontal line through D. In right triangle OLA, sin 30° = OL/OA, so 1/2 = OL/200 and OL = 100 m: the bird flies 100 m above the ground. Since LM = FD = 50 m, OM = OL − LM = 100 − 50 = 50 m. In right triangle OMD, sin 45° = OM/OD, so 1/√2 = 50/OD and OD = 50√2 = 50 × 1.414 ≈ 70.7 m. The bird is about 70.7 m from Deepak.

items.stem: As observed from the top of a 100 m high light house from the sea-level, the angles of depression of two ships are 30° and 45°. If one ship is exactly behind the other on the same side of the light house, find the distance between the two ships. [Use √3 = 1.732]
items.answer: Let AB be the light house of height 100 m with B at sea level, and let C and D be the ships, C the nearer one seen at 45° and D the farther one seen at 30°. In right triangle ABC, tan 45° = AB/AC — taking BC as the horizontal distance of the nearer ship, 1 = AB/BC gives BC = AB = 100 m. In right triangle ABD, tan 30° = AB/BD, so 1/√3 = AB/(BC + CD), giving BC + CD = √3 AB. Hence CD = √3 AB − AB = AB(√3 − 1) = 100(1.732 − 1) = 100 × 0.732 = 73.2 m. The two ships are 73.2 m apart.

items.stem: From the top of tower, 100 m high, a man observes two cars on the opposite sides of the tower with the angles of depression 30° and 45° respectively. Find the distance between the cars. (Use √3 = 1.73)
items.answer: Let DC be the tower of height CD = 100 m with D its foot, and let A and B be the cars on opposite sides, A seen at a depression of 30° and B at 45°. Put AD = x and DB = y. In right triangle ADC, tan 30° = CD/AD, so 1/√3 = 100/x and x = 100√3. In right triangle BDC, tan 45° = CD/DB, so 1 = 100/y and y = 100 m. Since the cars are on opposite sides, the distance between them is AB = AD + DB = 100√3 + 100 = 100 × 1.73 + 100 = 173 + 100 = 273 m. The cars are 273 m apart.
items.section_heading: FIVE MARKS QUESTIONS | Board Term-2 SQP 2016

items.stem: The angle of elevation of the top B of a tower AB from a point X on the ground is 60°. At point Y, 40 m vertically above X, the angle of elevation of the top is 45°. Find the height of the tower AB and the distance XB.
items.answer: Let AB be the tower with A at its foot on the ground, X the point on the ground and Y the point 40 m vertically above X. Draw YC horizontal to meet the tower at C, so YC = XA and CA = XY = 40 m; let BC = x, so AB = x + 40. In right triangle YCB, tan 45° = BC/YC, so 1 = x/YC and YC = x = XA. In right triangle XAB, tan 60° = AB/XA, so √3 = (x + 40)/x, giving √3 x − x = 40 and x = 40/(√3 − 1) = 20(√3 + 1) = 20√3 + 20. Hence AB = x + 40 = 20√3 + 60 = 20(√3 + 3) ≈ 94.64 m. For XB, in right triangle XAB, sin 60° = AB/BX, so √3/2 = AB/BX and BX = 2AB/√3 = 2 × 20(√3 + 3)/√3 = 40(1 + √3) = 40 × 2.73 ≈ 109.20 m. The tower is 20(√3 + 3) ≈ 94.64 m high and XB ≈ 109.20 m.
items.section_heading: FIVE MARKS QUESTIONS | Board Term-2 OD 2016

items.stem: A vertical tower stands on a horizontal plane and is surmounted by a flagstaff of height 5 m. From a point on the ground the angles of elevation of top and bottom of the flagstaff are 60° and 30° respectively. Find the height of the tower and the distance of the point from the tower. (take √3 = 1.732)
items.answer: Let AB be the tower of height x with B at its foot, AC the flagstaff of height 5 m, and P the point on the ground with BP = y. The bottom A of the flagstaff is seen at 30°, so in right triangle ABP, AB/BP = tan 30°, that is x/y = 1/√3, giving y = √3 x. The top C is seen at 60°, so in right triangle CBP, (x + 5)/y = tan 60° = √3. Substituting y = √3 x gives (x + 5)/(√3 x) = √3, so x + 5 = 3x and x = 2.5 m. Then y = √3 × 2.5 = 2.5 × 1.732 = 4.33 m. The tower is 2.5 m high and the point is 4.33 m from its foot.
items.section_heading: FIVE MARKS QUESTIONS | Board Term-2 Foreign 2016

items.stem: Two post are k metre apart and the height of one is double that of the other. If from the mid-point of the line segment joining their feet, an observer finds the angles of elevation of their tops to be complementary, then find the height of the shorted post.
items.answer: Let CD = h be the shorter post and AB = 2h the taller one, with their feet C and A a distance CA = k apart, and let M be the mid-point of CA, so CM = MA = k/2. Let the elevation of D from M be θ; since the two elevations are complementary, the elevation of B from M is 90° − θ. In right triangle AMB, AB/AM = tan(90° − θ) = cot θ, so 2h/(k/2) = 4h/k = cot θ. In right triangle CMD, CD/CM = tan θ, so h/(k/2) = 2h/k = tan θ. Multiplying the two results, (4h/k)(2h/k) = cot θ × tan θ = 1, so 8h²/k² = 1 and h² = k²/8. Hence h = k/(2√2) = k√2/4. The shorter post is k√2/4 metres high.
items.section_heading: FIVE MARKS QUESTIONS | Board Term-2 Foreign 2015

items.stem: A man on the top of a vertical tower observes a car moving at a uniform speed towards him. If it takes 12 min. for the angle of depression to change from 30° to 45°, how soon after this, the car will reach the tower?
items.answer: Let AB be the tower of height h with B its foot, and let the car move from P (depression 30°) to Q (depression 45°). In right triangle ABQ, tan 45° = AB/BQ, so 1 = h/BQ and BQ = h. In right triangle APB, tan 30° = AB/PB, so 1/√3 = h/(x + h) where PQ = x, giving x + h = h√3 and x = h(√3 − 1). The car covers PQ = h(√3 − 1) in 12 minutes, so its speed is h(√3 − 1)/12 m/min. The distance still to be covered is BQ = h, so the time needed is t = h ÷ [h(√3 − 1)/12] = 12/(√3 − 1) = 12(√3 + 1)/2 = 6(√3 + 1) = 6 × 2.73 = 16.38 minutes. The car reaches the tower about 16.38 minutes after the second observation.
items.section_heading: FIVE MARKS QUESTIONS | Board Term-2 OD 2014
